openQuestions: The Gate 1 no-hit rate is unmeasured, so the fraction of prompts a no-hit-only trigger would serve is unknown.
pickProb calibration (mean 0.641) is observed but not validated for a confidence threshold.
Run-to-run variance is unknown until a repeat run exists.
The 6 gold-less paraphrase probes are dropped from the denominator; which cases, and why, is unrecorded.

keyFindings.summary: The keep's binding condition is the margin: A-B=29 over a 25.6-row floor (3.4 rows of slack); a four-row swing flips the verdict.
Margin and sign test score the same quantity: A-B is identically W-L, so the rule's four conditions are not independent evidence.
The 256 questions are a hash-ordered 20-per-track sample of packet descriptions (256 of 1,727 usable); 85 percent of usable text is discarded and small tracks rest on as little as one row.
Questions are descriptions, not Gate 1 prompts; on the 14 gold-bearing paraphrase probes ripgrep beats Jev 8-2 and Jev abstains on 9.
Both baselines are structurally handicapped: lookup needs 80 percent single-phrase coverage with own-folder self-exclusion (17/256); ripgrep counts token presence by file plurality (68/256).
Zero of the 57 none-modal rows had the gold track picked in any order; decided-subset accuracy is 48.7 percent. Abstentions are lost, not latent.
Summing recorded pickProb across orders instead of the modal key raises A from 97 to 98 with no losses; the probability fields are recorded but never scored.
Per-call payload is ~1,118 tokens, 96.8 percent option block; a 5-option two-stage shortlist would cut input ~68 percent (call-shape amendment).
Option rotation is not a material accuracy tax: per-order right counts 94/95/96, abstains 58/56/57.
Rows are 16 heterogeneous clusters, not 256 exchangeable draws: per-track accuracy 0.15-1.00, abstention 0-0.80, sk-design alone 16/20 abstains.
The row set is unpinned: report stores counts only, calls store no question text, questions are re-derived per run, fixture promptSetHash is never checked.
Out-dir reuse truncates calls.jsonl and overwrites report.json; already logged as an unchased P2 in the 017 session.
The judgment is served nowhere; Gate 1 (all runtimes plus /speckit:search, which declares semantic matching unsupported) is the highest-reach insertion.

Sibling surfaces already apply the same judgment and pattern: spec-folder suggestion (keep K=40 A=39 B=30), clarify default (keep K=54 A=28 B=15), advisor suggested-order (probability aggregation, 2,200 ms budget), injection screen and completion claims.

Default-on needs a caller policy, not plumbing: cli-jev transport and JEV_TRANSPORT exist; D1 (dormant unless auth passes, no secret) governs availability; a call at p50 330 ms roughly doubles the 200 ms lookup budget.

The verdict is bound to jev 0.6.2/official/jev-1.13.0 and the hashed option set; requalification is print-only, so rollout needs an explicit trigger. Wrong picks (37.9 percent row / 48.7 percent decided) are the dominant product risk.
